_doc: WED-ACQ2 / P1.7 automatic corpus expansion (records/wed-acq2-auto-corpus-expansion-plan.md). Read by vera/acq_config.py. The feature is OFF unless `enabled` is exactly true AND the kill-switch env var is not true-like AND both DB env vars are set. Env var NAMES only; values are never read except to build engines and never logged.
_calibration_note: Capacity and cost bounds below are planner priors (not decision thresholds). The only decision gate (relevance) reuses config/fulldoc_answer.json admission thresholds unchanged. Calibrate from the first live job log lines (reason-code counts and stage durations only) - plan DV-2.
question_text: VERA-DAR automatic acquisition (open-access full text; visitor question not stored)

triggers._note: plan s11 V1: classifier_malformed never triggers; layer-1 injection/deny patterns are re-run on the question before enqueue

scope_expansion._dar1021_note: DAR-1021: a layer-2 decline starts acquisition (and, only when override_layer2_declines is true, may later be answered from acquired documents alone through the unchanged full-document admission, claim check and citation path) ONLY when the classifier's category is in layer2_categories_allowed (closed enum; missing or unknown = no). Layer-1 declines, malformed replies, other categories and layer2_none never acquire or answer. UNCALIBRATED: the classifier's category accuracy has not been measured on live traffic.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note: VERA-DAR found and added these documents while answering this question.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_stored: VERA-DAR answered from open-access documents it had already added to its collection for an earlier question.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_answer_only: VERA-DAR found these documents while answering this question and used them for this answer only; they had too few relevant passages to be added to its collection.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_mixed: VERA-DAR answered from documents it found or already held; some of the documents it found while answering this question had too few relevant passages to be added to its collection and were used for this answer only.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_unsaved: VERA-DAR found these documents while answering this question; they could not be saved to its collection.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_none: VERA-DAR searched for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but none passed its licence, content and relevance checks.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_deadline: VERA-DAR searched for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but could not finish checking them within its time limit.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_search_failed: VERA-DAR tried to search for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but the search did not complete.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_capped: VERA-DAR could not search for open-access full-text documents on this question right now because its hourly or daily search limit has been reached; no background search was started. Please try again later.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_doc_cap: VERA-DAR searched for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but could not check new documents because its daily document limit has been reached; no background search was started.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_unanswered: VERA-DAR searched for and checked open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but could not produce a checked answer from them.
scope_expansion.override_answer_prefix: The answer below comes only from open-access documents VERA-DAR added to its collection automatically after licence, content and relevance checks; it may be wrong. For medical, legal, financial or safety matters, please consult a qualified professional or an appropriate official source.
scope_expansion.reading_list_notice_answering: VERA-DAR has started a background search for open-access full-text sources on this question. If any pass its licence, content and relevance checks, asking the same question again in about ten minutes may give an answer drawn only from those documents.
scope_expansion.reading_list_notice_listing: VERA-DAR has started a background search for open-access full-text sources on this question. Documents that pass its licence, content and relevance checks may be added to its collection and used to answer later questions.
scope_expansion._note: plan s11 V1: answering a declined question from acquired documents ships OFF until the router returns a category enum (owner decision OD-1, P1.8). When true, only an off-domain (never deny/injection/malformed) decline whose ACQUIRED-only corpus admits >= admission thresholds is answered.

search._providers_note: plan D-3 + s11 V9: openalex only by default (Europe PMC refuses preprints, so arXiv candidates yield nothing; add "arxiv" to opt in); duckduckgo_lite excluded (no DOI/licence, shared daily cap, query-keyed cache). Provider instances are the /ask chain's cached instances (shared rate gates).

openalex_profile._note: ACQ-SEARCH-1021 (acquisition only; /ask unchanged). filter: OpenAlex works held by PubMed Central (source S2764455111), the only place Europe PMC full text comes from. and_extra_max/generic_terms: when the question has no core phrase, AND the distinctive terms instead of OR-ing every token (OR let ambiguous 'mma' match alpha-gal papers). No model call. Remove the block to restore the previous query.

ddg_first._note: YIELD-1021 (owner 2026-10-21: "ddg should be the first source for prompts/queries that are not in the corpus"). Acquisition and inline only. The shared /ask DuckDuckGoLiteProvider (its cache, daily_query_cap and gate, config search.duckduckgo_lite in vera_eval_run.json) runs concurrently with OpenAlex and Europe PMC; a result becomes a candidate ONLY via a scholarly identifier (DOI in the URL, PMC/PubMed link via one Europe PMC id lookup, arXiv id, or the citation_doi meta tag of a portal landing page fetched once, public-address checked, <= landing_max_bytes, <= landing_timeout_s, at most max_landing_fetches) and then passes the UNCHANGED resolve, fetch and licence gates; DDG-mapped candidates rank first. Every other page is held (never ingested or used as evidence). Planner priors, uncalibrated. enabled=false restores the previous search.

europepmc.query_suffix: OPEN_ACCESS:y AND HAS_FT:y AND NOT SRC:PPR AND NOT LICENSE:"cc by-nd" AND NOT LICENSE:"cc by-nc-nd"
europepmc._note: YIELD-1021: second metadata search, acquisition only (never the /ask reading list): Europe PMC lite search for open-access works with Europe PMC full text, merged with OpenAlex de-duplicated by DOI or PMCID; hits still resolve through the unchanged resolve_oa (by DOI; PLAN-NONDOI-1022: hits without a DOI resolve by PMCID, and only hits with neither are R-ACQ-NODOI). One search call. enabled=false removes it.

search._openalex_quota_note: YIELD-1021: after an OpenAlex HTTP 429 / budget error (keyless free tier = a small daily budget shared per IP, observed exhausted 2026-10-21 by BENCH-1021 and this task's live check) the acquisition search skips OpenAlex for this many seconds (process-wide; DDG and Europe PMC still run; the job makes one OpenAlex attempt, max_retries 1, so no Retry-After sleep). Planner prior, uncalibrated: lower it once a key (optional env OPENALEX_API_KEY, never logged) is set. Counted as openalex_429 / openalex_skipped_quota in the 'autoacq sources' log line.

bounds._docs_per_day_note: OWNER DECISION 2026-10-22 (verbatim, relayed by the orchestrator to DAR-TRACE-1022): "abolish the 20-a-day limit". null = no daily document cap (vera.acq_config.docs_per_day_cap); the RO daily count is not read. Still bounded by jobs_per_hour 6, jobs_per_day 30 and max_docs_per_job 2 (at most 60 documents/day). A number restores the cap.
bounds._max_search_calls_note: YIELD-1021: 2 -> 5 = OpenAlex 2 (AND profile + OR retry) + DuckDuckGo 1 + Europe PMC 1 + Europe PMC id lookup for DDG PMC/PubMed links 1. A lower value drops the later ones in that order (vera.search_providers.acquisition_search). INT-1022-B (orchestrator disposition 2026-10-22, owner may override): 5 -> 6 adds ONE slot for the Wikipedia reference portal (config/wiki_ref_portal.json; identifiers only, never evidence), taken after Europe PMC and before the id lookup, so the lookup keeps its slot (DAR-TRACE-1022's Europe PMC OR retry shares the lookup slot). This is an outbound search budget, not an acquisition cap: every candidate still passes the unchanged resolve, licence, injection, relevance and admission gates. Calibration: work/wikiref-1022/INTEGRATION.md 'Observed shapes', 3 live sample questions on 2026-10-22: the portal used 1 MediaWiki request each (0.4-0.65 s, one sample each), within its own budget.max_requests_per_question 4; candidates 20/0/2 (all DOI). Not a latency or yield calibration (3 samples). What would change it: 'autoacq sources' wiki_raw and cand_wikipedia_portal counts and the per-portal ratelimit log over a week of live jobs (drop back to 5 if the portal adds no stored documents).
bounds._acq_round_max_open_note: ROUNDS-1028: upper bound on simultaneously open per-topic acquisition rounds held in process (vera/acq_rounds.py); beyond it the least recently updated open round is evicted (its count is lost; DV-ACQ-FLOOR6-1 family). A memory bound, not a decision threshold, and no cap, admission or serving effect.
bounds._acq_round_target_note: FLOOR6-1028 INTERIM (vera/acq_rounds.py; owner 2026-10-28 verbatim: "Really, it should be: as each round of topic addition (initial or subsequent) should target at least 6 new docs. If there simply are not 6 more new docs to be found, that's a resource limitation, not a process failure."; OD-1027(4)). Every acquisition round for a micro-topic targets at least this many NEW stored documents; outcome met (>= target) or resource_limited (routes exhausted below target; not an error). Job caps unchanged (jobs_per_hour 6, jobs_per_day 30, max_docs_per_job 2), so a round of 6 spans >= 3 jobs. 6 is owner-declared, NOT calibrated (plan s24 Wilson note: half-width <= 0.10 at p 0.75 needs n about 70). Round state is in-process only (lost on restart) until the 010 acq_jobs table carries a round field; wired observationally by ROUNDS-1028 (topic key = read-time micro_topic anchor key, else unassigned; DV-ACQ-FLOOR6-1).
bounds._served_topic_balanced_note: FLOOR6-1028 (owner 2026-10-28, verbatim: "btw, 6 docs isn't a ceiling, it's a floor. statistically, 3/5 is only 60%, and 1/5 is only 20%. we need the tails smaller and the middle closer to 65%-85%"; corrected the same day: "Really, it should be: as each round of topic addition (initial or subsequent) should target at least 6 new docs. If there simply are not 6 more new docs to be found, that's a resource limitation, not a process failure."; OD-1027(4)). Serving has NO per-topic ceiling: served_per_topic_max null; served_topic_balanced true keeps the topic-balanced ORDER (round-robin across read-time micro-topic keys, topics by newest member, newest first within a topic, an unkeyed row its own topic), so only the global totals bind (served_acquired_max 30, served_acquired_max_bytes 50000000; raising them is an owner decision, work/acq-1027/plan.md s24). The 6 applies to ACQUISITION rounds (acq_round_target_new_docs), not to serving. Rollback: served_per_topic_max 6 restores the A4 ceiling; served_topic_balanced false with a null ceiling restores newest-N.
bounds._served_per_topic_note: SUPERSEDED in part by FLOOR6-1028 (_served_topic_balanced_note: no per-topic ceiling). ACQ S4-0 L9 (PD-1, G-SERVE). Serve the acquired corpus per micro-topic instead of the newest N by source_id: at most this many documents per read-time micro-topic key (vera.micro_topic), taken round-robin across topics newest topic first, total still capped by served_acquired_max / served_acquired_max_bytes (rebuild cost unchanged). A document with no assignable key counts as its own topic. null or absent = the previous newest-N behaviour (rollback). CAP6-1028: 3 -> 6 on the basis of owner declaration OD-1027(4) (records/decisions.md): "for statistical analysis, we really need at least 6 docs per micro-topic" (supersedes the S4-0 planner prior of 3, which was PROVISIONAL, DV-ACQ-6 family). Real-data state 2026-10-28: 63 stored documents in total; the per-micro-topic distribution is UNMEASURED (owner-run count pending, G0), so this is an owner-declared requirement, NOT a calibrated threshold. Interaction: the total caps are unchanged (served_acquired_max 30, served_acquired_max_bytes 50000000), so raising the per-topic cap adds no rebuild cost; round-robin still gives every topic its first document before any topic its second, so at most 30 / 6 = 5 topics can reach 6 served documents at once, and with 63 stored documents at most 30 are served. A topic with fewer than 6 stored documents is served in full. What would change it: the per-key document counts of the stored rows (owner-authorised SELECT) showing how many topics hold >= 6 documents, rebuild timing at the cap, and any owner decision to raise served_acquired_max (incremental indexing, plan OM-4, needed beyond about 50 documents).
bounds._served_scan_note: L9: at most this many newest acquired rows are indexed (source_id and provenance only, no content) to choose what to serve; a bound, not a decision threshold.
bounds._inline_fresh_docs_note: ACQ S4-0 L4b-0 (B3 fix). Fresh-acquisition budget of one inline pass. Equal to max_docs_per_job (the current cap, so no cap is raised); documents answered from stored rows (reuse) no longer reduce it. Capped by the remaining daily budget as before.
bounds._answer_min_admitted_spans_note: ONE-SPAN-1021 (owner approval 2026-10-21, DAR single-passage answer eligibility): on the inline answer path a fetched document with >= this many qualifying passages (after the unchanged licence, integrity, injection, harmful-content and relevance checks) supplies evidence to the EPHEMERAL answer corpus of this request only. Every sentence is still claim-checked against its cited passage and removed when unsupported; a partly covered question is answered as partial (claim_check.answer_completeness). Code floor 1 (0 qualifying passages never answers: reading list). Calibration: same data as _min_admitted_spans_note (work/wed-acq2/measure/measure-out.json, 9 real DAR-9 texts): at >= 1 span on-topic passes 7 of 17 (vs 5 at >= 2), off-topic false passes 2.6% (vs 2.2%), off-corpus probes 14.8% (vs 7.4%). Value 1 is the owner decision; the higher probe false-pass rate is bounded by the per-claim check (unsupported sentences removed) and by not persisting such documents. Change it when live ACQ-ANSWER-ONLY counts and reviewed single-passage answers show the per-claim check does not contain the false passes.
bounds._persist_min_admitted_spans_note: ONE-SPAN-1021: persistent-corpus admission, unchanged value (was min_admitted_spans; the calibration note below applies). A document below it may answer the request (answer_min_admitted_spans) but is NOT written (telemetry persisted=false, reason below_persist_min). The background job persists only at >= this value. Code floor 2 (owner).
bounds._min_admitted_spans_note: (applies to persist_min_admitted_spans) calibration 2026-10-21 (work/wed-acq2/measure/measure-out.json): single-document admission over the 9 real DAR-9 texts. calset-v2 on-topic (question, source doc) pairs: 17, of which >=1 span 7, >=2 5, >=3 4. Off-topic pairs (calset question vs other doc): 230, >=1 6 (2.6%), >=2 5 (2.2%), >=3 2 (0.9%). B2 off-corpus probes x 9 docs: 54, >=1 8 (14.8%), >=2 4 (7.4%), >=3 3 (5.6%). Value 2: halves the probe false-pass rate of 1 at a cost of 2 of 7 on-topic passes; 3 loses another on-topic pass for a small further gain. The gate is conservative (most on-topic pairs admit 0 spans) and not clean (2-7% false passes): residual R-7/FM-13. Change it when live R-ACQ-FEWSPANS/IRRELEVANT counts and stored-document reviews show a different trade-off.
bounds._served_acquired_max_note: measured 2026-10-21 (work/wed-acq2/measure/measure-out.json, measure2-out.json; dev machine, CPU only): acquired-corpus rebuild = verify + DarCorpus index 20 docs 64.5 s + evidence index 63.3 s; 30 docs 75.9 s + 77.5 s; 50 docs 141 s; 100 docs 230 s (index only). For scale, the existing 9-document base corpus costs 45.6 s + 45.9 s. 30 keeps one background rebuild at about the base corpus's own cost; more needs incremental indexing (plan OM-4). Rebuilds run off the request path and at most once per refresh_ttl_s.

inline._doc: DAR-INLINE-1021: inline acquisition inside the /ask request, off-topic override path only (vera/inline_acquire.py). Counts against bounds.jobs_per_hour, jobs_per_day and docs_per_day; uses max_candidates_resolved, max_docs_per_job and fetch_timeout_s unchanged; answers at bounds.answer_min_admitted_spans and persists at bounds.persist_min_admitted_spans (ONE-SPAN-1021). enabled=false restores the background-only behaviour.
inline._in_scope_note: DAR-INLINE-1021-R2 must-have 1: an IN-SCOPE question whose full-document result is insufficient or corpus_unusable (including while the base warm-up runs, must-have 2) also acquires inline, through the same gates, caps, kill switch and claim check; the answer uses the normal in-scope wording (no off-topic prefix). Layer-1 denies and injection hits never acquire. false = in-scope keeps the background trigger only.
inline._p0_5_note: P0-5-ACQ (owner decisions D1-D5, 2026-10-22; vera/acq_discovered.py). BOTH FLAGS SHIP OFF; enabling either is a separate owner decision (D5). use_discovered: the request's own cached discovery results (reading-list search) also become acquisition candidates (index licence dropped; deterministic Gate A; unchanged resolve/fetch/licence/injection/relevance/admission gates; per-record outcome in inline_acquisition.discovered; provenance.acquisition.discovery/url_chain/gate_a/gate_b/retention). landing_route (needs use_discovered): ONE bounded DOI -> landing -> JATS XML attempt within the landing_route host allowlists when Europe PMC has no open-access record. discovered_max 6: a candidate-count cap equal to bounds.max_candidates_resolved (planner prior, not a decision threshold; uncalibrated: no live run of this path exists; change it from live 'discovered' outcome counts).
inline._reuse_note: DAR-INLINE-1021-R2: ranked candidates already stored as acquired documents (and not tried by the stored-corpus attempt) are answered from their stored rows, read-only, re-verified at read (marker, every JATS licence element, injection re-scan, hashes) and never re-fetched or re-stored; they fill max_docs_per_job first and are not capped by docs_per_day (nothing new is acquired). DAR-TRACE-1022: a reused row must first pass THIS question's per-document relevance gate (answer_min_admitted_spans, same admission as a fresh document); a failing row is counted R-ACQ-REUSE-IRRELEVANT (R-ACQ-REUSE-UNUSABLE when the reader refuses it), does not use up max_docs_per_job and is not re-acquired. The previous accepted divergence (no relevance gate on reuse) is closed.
inline._calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED against live. deadline_s 45 covers search through the parallel fetch and gates; persist (measured 0.06 s; statement_timeout 15 s per statement) and the ephemeral corpus build (0.08-0.3 s) run after it. CMF-1022 retry guard (ask_service.inline_need_s): ONE request-level deadline (handler entry + public_mode.ASK_TIMEOUT_S 180 s, shared by every provider of the chain, at most one inline search per request) and the in-scope inline RETRY starts only if remaining >= deadline_s 45 + 3 x chain timeout_s 20 (writer + claim check + a second claim-check call) + 2 x grounding deadline_s 10 (reading-list fallback) = 125 s (this equals the worst path below, excluding the classifier already spent); an unreadable term skips the retry (inline_acquisition status budget_unknown), a short budget skips it (status deadline). The 15 s margin is not applied (180 s, not 165 s). RESIDUAL GAP: the 180 s is enforced only by the client; the server does not terminate a request. Budget against the UI's 180 s timeout with a 15 s margin (165 s): classifier <= 20 s (ask-provider-chain timeout_s) + inline <= 45 s + answer writer <= 20 s + claim check <= 20 s per call + reading-list fallback <= 2 x 10 s (grounding deadline_s, rl3 AND then OR) = 125 s worst single-call path, leaving 40 s for a second claim-check call. Measured locally 2026-10-21 (work/dar-inline-1021/e2e/logs/stage_inline_run1.json, run2.json; isolated PG16, real OpenAlex + Europe PMC, classifier/answer/claim-check LLM stubbed; boxing/MMA question): inline total 5.3 s and 6.3 s (search 1.5/1.2 s, parallel fetch+gates 3.5/4.8 s, write 0.06 s, ephemeral corpus 0.15/0.08 s). So 45 s is about 7x the measured cold path; lower it when live 'autoacq inline' ms_total lines show the spread, raise it only with the budget above. per_doc_timeout_s 25 (>= fetch_timeout_s 20 plus resolve), fetch_workers 4 (evaluate up to max_candidates_resolved 6 at once, admit at most max_docs_per_job), max_concurrent 2 (server-wide inline acquisitions; CPU-light, network-bound; planner prior), max_waiters 4 and waiter_wait_s 45 (identical in-flight questions; = deadline), result_ttl_s 600 (outcome reuse for provider-chain retries and repeats until the background refresh serves the stored documents): planner priors, not decision gates.

micro_topic._note: ACQ S4-0 L2/L2b. Read-time micro-topic key only; nothing is written (PD-3). anchor_bm25 is a PROVISIONAL prior (plan DV-ACQ-6), NOT calibrated: the frozen 200-document reference sample does not exist offline (no raw sources in the repo), so the IDF snapshot is built from the anchor texts only; a mis-assigned key only changes which stored documents are served first, never the total cap. k5.enabled false: no question-derived query leaves in S4-0.

judge._note: TOPICJUDGE-1028 (OD-1028(54): G2, live calibration; OD-1028(57): shadow never blocks). OFF by default (enabled must be literally true, and registration_enabled must be true too). A free Groq model (vera.inference_chain free entries, price 0 only) judges the draft against EVERY active/retired topic (no shortlist, no candidate-count cap; refused-category placeholder rows are never candidates, OD-1028(56)), run BEFORE the advisory lock, in batches of batch_size. COST GROWS WITH REGISTRY SIZE: ceil(candidates / batch_size) calls per registration; candidates beyond max_calls_per_registration or max_tokens_per_registration get the verdict unknown and the coverage (judged of total) is logged. Raise the budgets as the registry grows. mode shadow (default once enabled) AND judge disabled: registration follows the S3 rule: an exact duplicate (same normalized key, or same normalized label as an active/retired/suspended/draft topic) writes nothing and returns state duplicate, anything else is activated; the judge verdicts (shadow, logged to vera_vjay.topreg_judgments for calibration) and the lexical similarity score are LOG-ONLY and never suspend or block. mode active: yes = suspended, all no = active, any unknown or topics changed during the call = stays draft (re-proposing the key re-judges the draft); the lexical stand-in is log-only. Every failure (timeout, refusal-shaped, malformed output, budget) = unknown. max_judgments_per_day is reserved under a short lock before any call (reservation rows). These are the judge OWN allowances: max_groq_tokens_per_job (0) caps acquisition jobs and is untouched. All numbers are PROVISIONAL, uncalibrated, and the live model behaviour is UNTESTED.

registry_table._note: TOPICREG-1028 (owner: a table means a database table). read_from_db: explicit true reads vera_vjay.topreg_topics (db/migrations/pending/011-DRAFT, NOT applied) and uses only state=active rows; the JSON seed is used only when to_regclass says the table is absent; any other DB error or an invalid table stops (fail closed). registration_enabled: explicit true lets vera.topic_registry.register_proposed_topic write a draft, then, unless the judge is in ACTIVE mode, applies the S3 rule (OD-1028(57)): an exact duplicate returns state duplicate and writes nothing, anything else becomes active. The lexical similarity score (similarity_max 0.50, PROVISIONAL; scope_router.description_similarity, stemmed Jaccard plus char trigrams, LEXICAL NOT SEMANTIC) is LOG-ONLY and never suspends. In judge ACTIVE mode the judge verdicts decide (see judge._note). A MATCH = semantic equivalence or paraphrase only; narrower or broader non-equivalent topics are distinct (OD-1028(49)). Default OFF. refused_state_map (PROVISIONAL, OD-1028(51)/(52)/(56)): object, refusal category code -> refused state, used by vera.topic_registry.ensure_refused_category (fixed placeholder rows only, no question text) and scrutiny_flag (category level only). Validated at load: every key must be a classifier category whose disposition is refuse, every value one of banned/prohibited/secrets. No code maps to secrets (secrets is admin-only) until a real secret-leak refusal code exists. Such rows are never loaded as active, never trigger acquisition and are never text-matched. app_roles (D11): the three group and three login role names that the 011 draft's psql-variable defaults also use (app_rw_login, app_wo_login, app_ro_login); validated at load; an -v override of those variables must be mirrored here. cache_ttl_seconds (accepted 0..3600, else rejected at load): how long the DB registry (or the absent-table fallback) is cached before it is re-read. proposal_state: app-proposed topics are written as draft (the DB trigger enforces it); only draft is accepted.

keys._note: ACQ S4-0 L1/L4c. Env var NAME only; the value is read at runtime from the process environment and never stored in tracked config (vera.acq_config.refuse_key_like_values refuses a config holding a key-like value).

serve._note: probe = one read-only SELECT; a changed signature starts ONE background rebuild (evidence index pre-warmed) with atomic swap; 300 s coalesces rebuilds

resolve._note: Open-access resolution by DOI through the Europe PMC REST search (core result). API shape from DAR-9 precedent and documentation knowledge; NOT live-verified (plan FM-11).

licence_url_map._note: Europe PMC licence strings (lower-cased, whitespace-collapsed) -> version-less CC family URL; never a guessed version; unmapped = hold

landing_route._note: P0-5 Step B (inline.landing_route, ships false). Exact host names only (no wildcards, no suffix matching), re-checked on every hop with https, no userinfo, port 443, the public-address check and robots.txt (fail closed). resolver_hosts are the DOI resolver; publisher_hosts are the owner-approved publisher hosts for landing pages AND JATS targets (the JATS URL must be on the same host as the final landing page). publisher_hosts SHIPS EMPTY: candidate hosts are pending owner sign-off after raw-HTML verification (work/demo-1022/p0-5/NOTES.md), so with the flag on and the list empty every landing route ends R-ACQ-HOST. Each publisher host must also be added to a config/rate_limits.json portal (and its robots crawl-delay honoured) before enabling. Planner priors, uncalibrated.

ingest_overlay._note: labels plus the non-DOI identity allowlist; every other fulltext_ingest filter runs unchanged
ingest_overlay.question_text: VERA-DAR automatic acquisition (open-access full text; visitor question not stored)

candidate.rationale_prefix: Automatic open-access full-text acquisition (WED-ACQ2). Gate A not applied; relevance = answer-path admission over the single document.

ingest_overlay._versioning: labels are bound to marker vera-dar-auto-acquire-v1; never edit in place (a change needs a new marker version; old rows keep their labels)
ingest_overlay._non_doi_note: PLAN-NONDOI-1022 (owner decision 2026-10-22: documents without a DOI are acceptable; Wikipedia is not a source): identity allowlist, not a label. It waives ONLY the doi requirement and doi_pattern for doi=null items whose identifier matches an anchored pattern here; every other filter (licence, embedded licence, injection at write and read, relevance, span minimums, reader re-check, claim check) is unchanged. A record that also carries a DOI (Europe PMC core record or the JATS article-id) is stored under the DOI identity instead. Only pmcid is listed: every acquired full text is fetched from Europe PMC by PMCID, so a PMID-only or arXiv-only record has no fetch path here. The marker stays v1: no existing row changes.
ingest_overlay._embedded_licence_note: WED-P17-VER item 4: an embedded licence that is present but not a recognised CC/CC0 licence is held (unclear = hold); applies to acquired documents only

injection_scan._note: applied to the converted full text at write AND at read for acquired documents; any match refuses the document (R-ACQ-INJECT); stored text is never edited
injection_scan._calibration_note: max_hits 0 (any match refuses). Measured 2026-10-21 over the 9 DAR-9 texts (work/wed-acq2/measure/injection-scan-base9.txt): 0 hits. Expected false positives in AI-security/AI-coding papers that quote injection strings (not in the sample); review R-ACQ-INJECT counts (plan FM-16).
